      Tetris - Free Online Browser Game

      Stack falling tetrominoes, clear lines, and survive the rising tempo.

      About Tetris

      Tetris on PixelGame delivers the legendary falling-block puzzle with hold, soft and hard drops, and rising tempo. Clear complete horizontal lines before the stack tops out. Since its 1980s debut, Tetris has defined spatial puzzle design; this browser edition keeps the muscle-memory controls players expect while wrapping them in PixelGame’s cyberpunk HUD. Play free online with zero downloads — ideal for Chromebook, desktop, and mobile browsers when you want a focused, high-skill solo session.

      Objective

      Clear lines without topping out.

      Keyboard & Touch Controls

      Controls for Tetris
      InputAction
      ← / →Move

      C HoldIn-game action

      How to Play

      1. Fit pieces to complete horizontal rows.
      2. Cleared rows score points.
      3. Hold a piece for later with C.
      4. Game ends when the stack reaches the top.

      Tetris FAQ

      Can I play Tetris on school or work Chromebooks?

      Yes. Tetris runs entirely in a modern web browser at pixelgame.games — no install, extension, or admin rights required. If your network allows HTTPS game sites, open the game page and play instantly on Chromebook, PC, or mobile.

      Does PixelGame require an account, download, or plugin?

      No. PixelGame is a pure HTML5 canvas arcade. There are no user accounts, no app downloads, and no Flash or Java plugins. Close the tab and the session vanishes.

      How do I play with friends using a room code?

      Tetris is a solo game. For multiplayer titles on PixelGame, open a multiplayer game page, choose Play With Friends, and share the room invite link or code.

      Does this game store my personal data or gameplay history?

      No accounts and no tracking databases. The only optional storage is a short-lived sessionStorage snapshot so a refresh can resume an active match; returning to the arcade grid clears it. PixelGame does not keep personal profiles or long-term gameplay history.
